title: Digital Agency for Miami Companies: AI, Web, Growth | 22 Signals
description: 22 Signals works with Miami companies on AI, cloud, data, web, apps, SEO, ads, video and 3D: one accountable lead, bilingual work, remote from London.
h1: A digital agency for Miami companies: AI, technology and marketing with one accountable lead
intro: 22 Signals is a London-based business solutions company working with established Miami companies. We build AI tools, cloud systems, data dashboards, websites and apps, then grow them with SEO, paid media, video and 3D. One Signal Lead owns your work, campaigns run in English and Spanish, and our day overlaps your Miami morning.

sections.h: Why Miami companies work with us
p: Miami's economy runs on a handful of strong sectors: real estate and property development, hospitality and tourism, trade and logistics with Latin America, finance and a growing crypto and fintech scene, private healthcare and aesthetics, and fashion and beauty. Most of the companies in them are well past the startup stage. They have staff, customers in two languages and a stack of tools that grew one vendor at a time.

What they usually lack is one team that owns the whole picture. A developer in Brickell might have a website from one agency, ads from a freelancer, renders from a studio abroad and a CRM nobody set up properly. When people search for a digital agency Miami companies can hand all of that to, they rarely find one that also builds AI and cloud systems. That combination, with one accountable lead, is what we offer.

sections.h: From Brickell to Coral Gables: who we work with
p: Miami's business districts each have their own buyers. Brickell is home to banks, wealth managers, law firms and crypto companies, and they care about security, compliance and a polished brand. Downtown mixes corporate offices, developers and public-sector contractors. Wynwood has creative studios, galleries and younger tech companies that care about visuals as much as code.

Coral Gables hosts regional offices of many multinational firms with Latin American operations, along with professional services firms and medical practices. Doral and the area around Miami International Airport are the city's logistics engine. We shape each engagement around the kind of company you are, not just the city you are in.

Spanish is spoken at home by a large share of Miami-Dade residents, and many Miami companies sell to buyers in Colombia, Venezuela, Argentina, Mexico and Brazil. Customers search, message and buy in English, Spanish or a mix of both.

A digital agency Miami customers respond to has to plan Spanish as its own piece of work rather than a translation pass at the end: separate pages and keywords, ad campaigns split by language, follow-ups in the customer's language, and AI tools tested on real Spanish messages. Portuguese is added where Brazilian buyers matter.

sections.h: Florida data and privacy rules, in plain words
p: The Florida Digital Bill of Rights has been in force since July 2024. Its full duties fall mainly on very large companies with over $1 billion in global revenue, but its rules on selling sensitive data reach further. The Florida Information Protection Act requires most businesses to notify affected people within 30 days of a breach, and the Florida Telephone Solicitation Act sets consent rules for marketing calls and texts.

We build those rules into the work: consent on forms, careful handling of patient and financial data, locked-down access and good logs. We are not a law firm, so we write things down clearly for your counsel to approve.

sections.h: How remote delivery works from London
p: Our head office is in London, and we work with Miami companies remotely. Miami runs on Eastern Time, five hours behind London, so our afternoon is your morning. Calls and reviews usually sit between 8am and 1pm Miami time, and work done in London is often waiting when your team logs on.

Every engagement follows the same process: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow. Every date agreed goes in writing. When a project needs us in the room, for a kick-off, a workshop or a shoot, we plan a visit when the project needs it.

We have worked with more than 30 companies across four regions, from US law firms and an aesthetics practice to a neurotech company, an esports business and a beauty salon. That range is why we can bring lessons from one sector into another, which is useful in a city as mixed as Miami.

Pick the service closest to your problem and read the Miami page for it, or book a 15-minute call. It is a fit check, not a pitch: we will tell you whether we are the right team and, if not, what we would do in your position. A digital agency Miami firms hire should be able to say that plainly.

faqs.q: Do you have an office in Miami?
faqs.a: No. Our head office is in London and we work with Miami companies remotely. Our working day overlaps your morning, calls are scheduled between roughly 8am and 1pm Miami time, and every date is agreed in writing. When a project needs us on site, we plan a visit when the project needs it.

faqs.q: Can you work in Spanish as well as English?
faqs.a: Yes. We plan websites, SEO, ads, video and AI tools for English and Spanish audiences from the start, with Portuguese where Brazilian buyers matter. Spanish content is treated as its own work rather than a quick translation, because Miami and Latin American customers notice the difference immediately.

faqs.q: What kinds of Miami companies do you work with?
faqs.a: Mainly established companies with 5 to 500 staff in real estate and development, hospitality, trade and logistics, finance and fintech, healthcare and aesthetics, and fashion and beauty. We also work with founders building new products, but most of the companies we work with already have customers, staff and systems.

faqs.q: How do you handle the time difference with Miami?
faqs.a: London is five hours ahead of Miami. We hold live calls in your morning, when both teams are online, and use our earlier start to build, test and prepare updates before your day begins. Your Signal Lead sends written updates, so progress never depends on catching someone on the phone.

faqs.q: Can you take over from our current agency or developer?
faqs.a: Yes. We start by reviewing what exists, from the website and ad accounts to cloud systems and data, and we fix urgent risks first. Then we agree what to keep and what to change. Access, logins and ownership are documented so you are never locked in to any vendor, including us.

faqs.q: How does Florida privacy law affect our marketing and data?
faqs.a: For most mid-sized companies, the main practical rules are consent for calls and texts, careful handling of sensitive data, and a 30-day breach notice duty. We build consent, access control and logging into websites, ads and automations, and document it for your lawyer to review.
